episodes.214732: During the late night/early overnight hours of August 5th/6th, storms brought damaging wind gusts to portions of Cass, Jackson, and Johnson Counties in western Missouri. A swath of 70-100 mph winds caused extensive tree damage and even some structure damage from the Raymore/Belton area, through the community of Creekmoor, and into Raintree Lake near the Cass/Jackson county line. The worst damage was along a roughly 6 mile long and 1 mile wide path along the Cass/Jackson County line from Kentucky Blvd in Raymore (near Creekmoor) into the western portions of Raintree Lake.
episodes.214746: A few widely scattered severe thunderstorms sparked by a lee surface trough produced localized wind damage in parts of northern Virginia.
episodes.214749: A few widely scattered severe thunderstorms sparked by a lee surface trough produced localized wind damage in parts of northern Virginia.
episodes.214750: A few thunderstorms ignited along a surface trough and the bay breeze, producing sporadic gale-force winds over portions of the waters.
episodes.214808: Deep moisture present in the atmosphere coupled with marginally sufficient shear and a shortwave trough allowed for some thunderstorm development during the evening hours of August 6, 2026. Storms across south-central Pennsylvania began to exhibit upscale growth due to the favorable shear, lift, and moisture in the atmosphere with a severe thunderstorm producing isolated tree damage and flash flooding in Cumberland County. Further southeast, thunderstorms across Lancaster County led to one person being struck by lightning.
episodes.214956: Scattered thunderstorms once again developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of August 6, 2026. These thunderstorms produced heavy rain, especially along the Cumberland Plateau. Reports of street flooding with one stuck vehicle were received in Cookeville.
episodes.214968: August heat and humidity allowed for a lone storm to reach severe levels in South Carolina.
episodes.215385: Thunderstorms developed in a very unstable atmosphere. There was enough flow for storms to be moving, but some storms trained over one another, resulting in isolated instances of flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of two to four inches were observed.
episodes.215760: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed across the Flint Hills during the evening hours of August 5th. Multiple bouts of large hail were reported ranging from quarter to golf ball size, mainly across Greenwood County.
episodes.216121: A severe thunderstorm moved through the Kachina Village area and produced some large hail.
episodes.216208: An area of low pressure tracked along a stationary front and produced flash flooding.
episodes.216211: An area of low pressure tracked along a stationary front and produced flash flooding.
episodes.216231: On the morning of August 5th, scattered showers were ongoing along the mountains of West Virginia, while a warm front lifted north through the area. More robust showers and thunderstorms developed in southeast Ohio and then progressed east across West Virginia as the decaying boundary was redirected across the area that afternoon into the night. Heavy downpours in thunderstorms deposited one to three inches of rain across portions of the state, which prompted instances of flooding in Kanawha and Upshur Counties. Primary impacts included flooding of a few roads and low spots.
episodes.216467: A cluster of storms over central South Carolina pushed northward into the Piedmont of central North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. Several storms became severe, producing numerous damaging wind reports.
episodes.216553: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northwestern Arkansas during the evening of the 6th, along an outflow boundary from earlier thunderstorm activity to the east. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.216692: During the late evening on 08/05, scattered storms developed and tracked across east central Kansas. A few storms produced large hail to golfball size in diameter.
episodes.217006: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.217235: A disturbance moved through the region as southerly winds transported warm, humid air into the area. Afternoon heating supported increasing instability, while enhanced mid-level winds allowed for scattered clusters of showers and thunderstorms to develop despite weak overall wind shear. Storms were capable of producing isolated damaging wind gusts, especially east of the Finger Lakes.
episodes.217706: A stalled frontal boundary to the northwest of the region, combined with the usual late summer daytime heating/influences of sea breezes, resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms across the area. Precipitable Water (PWAT) values reached as high as 2.2 to 2.5 inches during this period, which strongly supported heavy rain and flooding potential.
episodes.217889: During the late night of the 6th into the early AM hours of the 7th, a complex of storms moved from north to south through the combined OK/TX Panhandles, entering the OK Panhandle first. As this complex moved through it produced thunderstorm winds damage in the OK Panhandle with winds continuing to be measured well above 60 mph by ground stations throughout the area. One isolated updraft produced hail up to the size of nickels near Boise City, OK. After the thunderstorm stopped, decaying showers continued to bring strong winds to the surface from aloft and strong winds continued to be measured by ground stations.
episodes.217933: Deep moisture and moderate levels of instability residing along the western periphery of high pressure centered across the Atlantic supported thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.217960: Scattered severe thunderstorms and flash flooding developed during the afternoon on 8/6 in a strongly unstable environment with generally weak flow aloft. Deep layer moisture and PWATs around 2 inches and weak storm motion with training and back building thunderstorms supported high rainfall rates and a flash flooding threat. Storms became widespread with many flash flood reports in the urban areas of Columbia and Augusta with multiple damaging wind reports scattered across the forecast area.
episodes.217961: Scattered severe thunderstorms and flash flooding developed during the afternoon on 8/6 in a strongly unstable environment with generally weak flow aloft. Deep layer moisture and PWATs around 2 inches and weak storm motion with training and back building thunderstorms supported high rainfall rates and a flash flooding threat. Storms became widespread with many flash flood reports in the urban areas of Columbia and Augusta with multiple damaging wind reports scattered across the forecast area.
episodes.218025: During the late evening hours of August 5th, storms brought damaging wind gusts and hail to portions of eastern KS, primarily Johnson County.
episodes.218068: Hot and humid conditions were in place across eastern New York on August 6-7, 2026. Heat index values reached between 95 and 100 degrees across portions of the Hudson Valley on August 6 with these values continuing into August 7 for portions of the mid-Hudson Valley. In addition, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed each afternoon into the early evening resulting in some incidents of wind damage as well as localized flash flooding.
episodes.218093: Slow-moving showers and thunderstorms created isolated flooding in areas. MRMS depicts 2 to 4 inches per hour rainfall rates in some areas.
episodes.218247: Thunderstorms fired along a low-level jet during the overnight hours of August 5th-6th. Ample instability and the persistent low-level jet allowed continuous development and subsequent training of thunderstorms in central and and east-central Missouri. Rain amounts upwards of 4 to 6 inches caused flash flooding in Boone and Franklin counties.
episodes.218335: An upper high over the southwest kept northeast flow over the region.  Low level moisture remained high with southeast surface winds up to the Rio Grande Valley.  Slow moving thunderstorms brought flash flooding to western El Paso County while thunderstorm wind gusts caused damage over the eastern portion of the county.
episodes.218355: Scattered thunderstorms and storms clusters developed across the western Carolinas throughout the afternoon. One storm became severe shortly after moving into Gaston County from South Carolina and produced sporadic damaging wind gusts. A series of slow-moving storm clusters produced very heavy rainfall and localized flash flooding in Rutherford and Polk Counties.
episodes.218498: Thunderstorms producing downpours resulted in flash flooding across New Jersey. Multiple cars were stuck in flood waters along with multiple water rescues.
episodes.218548: Easterly sea breeze flow produced afternoon convection that produced strong marine wind gusts from around Crystal River southward through the Tampa and Sarasota Bay waters.
episodes.218584: The active monsoon period continued with severe thunderstorms, hail and flash flooding, primarily on Pima and Cochise Counties. Recorded thunderstorm wind gusts ranged from 59-69 mph that knocked down 40 power poles in Three Points, 9 power poles in Tucson, and lifted and moved a shed in the east side of Tucson. Severe hail occurred in Bisbee that resulted in damage to windows due to 1 inch diameter hail. Due to the locally heavy rainfall, there was 2 swift water rescues, one in Three Points and one in the SE side of Tucson with no injuries reported. Additionally, another swift water rescue in Greenbush Draw that resulted in a fatality with no body recovered.
episodes.218590: Moderately strong high pressure centered offshore the Mid Atlantic Coast produced a deep, easterly moist flow across the Florida Keys coastal waters with little if any convective inhibition.  Clusters of showers and thunderstorms of short duration produced scattered gale-force wind gusts along the Lower and Upper Florida Keys.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed across central Polk County after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell in just a couple of hours. Impacted roads inundated by a combination of poor drainage and small stream flooding included Sykuka Rd and Hayes Rd. A residence on Hayes Rd was briefly isolated due to significant driveway flooding. The most significant flooding was reported near the intersection of Burgundy Ln and Highway 14, where the road was inundated with around 2 feet of water from Hughes Creek.

A tree was down blocking the entire road on Grace Quarters Road. Given the lack of other damage in the area, ongoing flash flooding, and nearby observations well below severe limits, it is unlikely that this tree fall was due to severe wind and was more likely due to extremely saturated ground (there were cars floating on the same street).
